knownStaleness.topic: Population shares and religious affiliation in Who We Are
knownStaleness.problem: The chapter's proportions are from the 2006 census era and the 2021 Census has moved all of them. The guide says First Nations are "about 65%" of Indigenous people (2021: 58.0%), that "about half" of First Nations people live on reserve (2021: 40.6% among status First Nations), and that "the great majority of Canadians identify as Christians" (2021: 53.3%, just over half). The last is the worst for a learning game: "No religion" is now 34.6%, larger than Catholic at 29.9%, so a question teaching the guide's framing punishes a learner who knows the current figure. Recorded at chapter grain for a few minutes on 2026-09-08, which forced volatile on all 46 questions in the chapter when three carry the shares — the same defect this register already had for the Oath, repeated by the same hand within the hour.
knownStaleness.action: volatile: never put one of these shares in an option or an explanation. The live page (who-are-canadians.html, Date modified 2025-08-08) still carries every one of them, so the modification date is not evidence of revision and re-fetching resolves nothing. Recorded here as prose first, which was the same defect ADR-0016 section 1 had already fixed: that sentence is a live check, and it has been transcribed into liveChecks[] where a gate can read it and where it expires. With it, Who We Are is on ADR-0016 section 2 row 2, so the volatile demand no longer fires on the fifteen questions that share pages 17, 18 and 21 with these shares and carry facts that will never move - treaty rights, the Royal Proclamation, residential schools, the 2008 apology, the meaning of "Inuit", Michif. bannedFromAnswers is the whole mitigation on row 2, and the clock that keeps it honest is liveChecks[].checkedAt, not a per-question re-fetch. Claim-level grain would still be finer than page grain, but it is no longer what this entry costs: page grain now over-reaches only into a term search, not into fifteen re-verifications.

knownStaleness.topic: The G8 and Russia's membership in Canada's Economy
knownStaleness.problem: Page 90 lists Russia among the G8. Russia was suspended in March 2014 and the group has met as the G7 ever since. Confirmed against the live page on 2026-09-09, Date modified 2025-04-11: it still names Russia, eleven years on.
knownStaleness.action: G7 is banned beside G8 deliberately: an option naming the G7 is right about the world and wrong about the document the exam is drawn from, so no answer may rest on the group's name in either direction. The flag stops at the G8 clause -- the same sentence's ranking claim is volatile's job, and folding it in would over-fire onto a usable proposition and repeat the grain defect this register keeps closing.

knownStaleness.topic: The English lyrics of O Canada
knownStaleness.problem: Page 84 prints "True patriot love in all thy sons command". Bill C-210 received royal assent on 2018-02-07 and replaced that line with "in all of us command". Confirmed against the live page on 2026-09-09, Date modified 2026-05-14 -- four months old -- still printing the pre-2018 line.
knownStaleness.action: Both the stale line and the current one are banned, for the reason G7 is banned beside G8. The two facts flanking it on the same page -- proclaimed 1980, first sung in Quebec City 1880 -- cannot move and are what the shipped questions grade.

knownStaleness.topic: NAFTA and its replacement in Canada's Economy
knownStaleness.problem: Page 90 says Mexico joined in 1994 in "the broader North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA)". NAFTA was replaced by CUSMA on 2020-07-01. The live page, Date modified 2025-04-11, still says NAFTA, so this is upstream and permanent -- the same disposition as the G8 entry beside it.
knownStaleness.action: Both the dead name and the current one are banned, for the reason G7 is banned beside G8: an option naming CUSMA is right about the world and wrong about the document the exam is drawn from. The two shipped questions on this sentence survive it, because they grade the year and the country rather than the agreement's name. Recorded and not flagged: the same sentence's "over 444 million people and over $1 trillion in merchandise trade in 2008" is a 2008 figure printed as current. Nothing cites it and nothing should.

knownStaleness.topic: The 2008 trade and population figures in Canada's Economy
knownStaleness.problem: Page 90 prints "over 444 million people and over $1 trillion in merchandise trade in 2008" as a present-tense description of North American free trade. It is an eighteen-year-old magnitude in the same sentence as NAFTA, which was replaced by CUSMA on 2020-07-01, so the sentence is stale twice over for two different reasons. Confirmed against the live page (canadas-economy.html, Date modified 2025-04-11) on 2026-09-09: it still prints the same 2008 figures. Nothing in the bank cites them today. ADR-0028 sends an author onto this page's neighbours looking for propositions, and a number in a sentence is the most quotable thing on a short page, so this is recorded before it is needed rather than after.
knownStaleness.action: No option or explanation may rest on a trade volume or a population total from this page, and that includes a corrected one: a 2026 figure is right about the world and wrong about the document the exam is drawn from, which is the reason G7 is banned beside G8 in the entry above. The teachable propositions in this sentence are the DATES and the PARTNERS -- free trade with the United States in 1988, Mexico joining in 1994 -- and both are already claimed. Ask about those or about nothing here.

liveChecks.consequence: IRCC has not revised Discover Canada for the accession. The live pages still read "Her Majesty is a symbol of Canadian sovereignty", "53 other nations", "Her Majesty's Loyal Opposition" and "308 electoral districts", and caption a photo "Queen Elizabeth II". So our cache is not drifting behind a maintained source: the source itself is unrevised, cache and live agree, and both are out of date. A drift-based quarantine has no trigger and re-fetching cannot resolve a stale fact. What makes the bank shippable is bannedFromAnswers, not a future fetch.
